assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint mechanism of Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) explains how small shocks are amplified and persist through credit limits tied to asset values. It is a core building block of macro-finance and of how the 2008 crisis and policy responses are understood. It is conceptually fundamental and has a large, lasting influence on research and on central-bank thinking.
assessment.attribution: The credit-cycles paper is a clear two-author contribution, so Kiyotaki and Moore are the natural pair. The financial-accelerator strand (Bernanke-Gertler, Gilchrist) overlaps, but Bernanke's 2022 prize partly covers it. Gertler and Gilchrist are therefore not proposed here.
assessment.maturity: About three decades have passed, with extensive theoretical, quantitative and empirical follow-up. Timing is mature and unlikely to be seen as premature.
uncertainties: How the Committee would weigh overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Whether Gertler or Gilchrist should be added for the quantitative financial-accelerator strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed trade theory and measurement. They introduced new channels for gains from trade (reallocation across firms, exporter selection) and moved the field to firm-level microdata. The framework also links closely to growth, productivity and misallocation research.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple extended it to FDI and exports, and Redding developed the welfare and spatial implications. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made parallel contributions that are not credited on this ballot, which complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across many countries and datasets. The framework is the standard in the field and is mature.
uncertainties: Parallel work by Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and by Eaton and Kortum, makes the right set of laureates unclear.
Helpman also appears on another ballot, so credit may be split across trade lines.
Redding's inclusion would depend on how the Committee weighs the spatial extensions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income series built from tax records reshaped the empirical study of inequality and public debate. The work provides new measurement and data infrastructure (the World Inequality Database) and has spawned a large literature. The theoretical interpretation, especially the r > g argument, is more contested than the data contribution.
assessment.attribution: The core measurement contribution is Piketty and Saez (2003) and their related work. Zucman's work on offshore wealth and wealth distribution is more recent and could be added or held back. Atkinson, now deceased, is not creditable.
assessment.maturity: The measurement work is over twenty years old and widely replicated. The most contested policy and theoretical claims are still debated.
uncertainties: Debate over measurement choices and the theoretical framework.
Whether Zucman's work is mature enough to include.
Whether the Committee prefers measurement over causal or theoretical advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are the workhorse of modern monetary-policy analysis. They underpin inflation targeting and rules-based policy, and they are central to how macroeconomists model stabilization.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is crowded. Calvo (staggered pricing) and Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) are foundational, and Woodford synthesized the framework and its normative analysis. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler made major quantitative and empirical contributions but cannot all be included under the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: The framework has several decades of use in policymaking and research, so maturity is high. Its performance during the post-2020 inflation episode is a recent test, though it also keeps the field relevant.
uncertainties: Eight credited names show how contested attribution is.
Alternative triples such as Woodford, Gali and Christiano are plausible.
Possible discomfort with the framework's limits in the financial crisis and the post-2020 inflation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) linked firm-level resource misallocation quantitatively to cross-country income and TFP differences. They created a measurement framework now widely used in growth, development and macro-IO research. The key question is how much of the income gap is due to misallocation rather than to technology or factor accumulation.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the central pair for the measurement framework. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) made a parallel theoretical contribution, and Rogerson is not credited on this ballot, so attribution is incomplete. Klenow is a long-running co-author of the evaluating member, which should be disclosed.
assessment.maturity: The approach is about fifteen years old, with extensive application but also critiques about measurement error and markup interpretation. It is reasonably mature but less settled than some other candidates.
uncertainties: Measurement-error and markup critiques may weaken the quantitative conclusions.
The missing Restuccia-Rogerson co-credit.
The evaluating member's collaboration with Klenow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work established modern political economics: how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It combines formal theory with systematic empirical evidence and has influenced the study of institutions, development and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clearest pair, through their book and papers on constitutions and policy. Besley's work on state capacity and political agency is closely related and complementary. The 2024 prize for institutions (Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson) overlaps in theme but not in specific contribution.
assessment.maturity: Developed over thirty years with strong replication and follow-up. Maturity is high, though a recent prize in the broad area could weigh against it.
uncertainties: Perceived overlap with the 2024 institutions prize.
Persson's role in the Committee's history and institutional ties, which the simulation discloses but does not adjudicate.
Whether Besley should be included alongside the pair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural demand estimation with differentiated products (BLP) made it possible to measure market power, merger effects and welfare in real industries. It is a methodological advance with very wide use in industrial organization, antitrust and regulation, and it spread into trade and other fields.
assessment.attribution: The BLP trio of Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes is the natural core, with Pakes also central to dynamic industry models (Ericson-Pakes, Bajari-Benkard-Levin). Bresnahan, Reiss and others made earlier or complementary contributions that make attribution wider.
assessment.maturity: BLP dates to the mid-1990s and has been used for three decades, so confirmation is extensive. The methodological advance itself is well established.
uncertainties: The line between methodology and the economic insight it delivers.
Whether Bresnahan or the dynamic-model contributors should be recognized instead.
A seven-name credited list shows contested attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Autor and co-authors changed how economists understand technology, trade and labour markets. The task-based approach and the China-shock evidence explain job polarization, local labour-market adjustment and wage inequality. The work has strong policy relevance and has changed the public debate on trade.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock evidence is Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The task framework builds on Autor, Levy and Murphy and on Acemoglu-Autor, and Acemoglu already shared the 2024 prize. Katz's earlier contribution on skill-biased change adds attribution complexity.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock papers are about a decade old, so maturity is moderate. The task approach is older and well established, but long-run interpretation of the trade effects is still being refined.
uncertainties: Debate over the size and persistence of the trade effects and over the identification strategy.
Overlap with the task-based literature associated with Acemoglu.
Whether Katz or Murphy-related contributions should be credited instead.
